title: Dedicated capacity buffering, SLA tiers, and failover credit experiments
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Run an experiment to validate a portfolio of dedicated capacity offerings that include low-latency guaranteed bands, a small pool of transferable 'buffer credits' for short overages, and explicit failover-credit rules to preserve service continuity at predictable economics for enterprise customers.
objective: Create a packaging and pricing matrix that balances predictable revenue (reserved GPU bands) with operational resilience (buffer/failover credits and controlled autoscale) and is acceptable to legal/SQ and enterprise procurement.
success_metrics: 1) Conversion rate of large trial accounts to reserved plans >= 18% within 90 days; 2) Average overage spend per customer <= 10% of reserved commit; 3) Number of production incidents caused by capacity shortfalls reduced by 60% for pilot customers; 4) NRR impact neutral or positive after 6 months.
proposed_pricing_variants: Variant A - SteadyBand: fixed reserved throughput tiers (S/M/L) with low price per token and no included buffer; overage at premium rate; SLA credit for availability below 99.9%.

Variant B - BufferPool: moderate reserved discount + monthly buffer credits (e.g., 10% of reserve) that auto-apply for short overages; overage beyond buffer billed at standard overage rate; includes limited failover lanes (lower-cost model) for saturation events.

Variant C - FlexReserve: smaller guaranteed band + burstable autoscale with pre-negotiated burst blocks (bought as monthly bundles) and higher latency SLOs during bursts; designed for customers who want lower base commit.
Variant D - Enterprise Continuity: custom reserved band + dedicated failover capacity and priority routing (SLA 99.95%) with premium price and 24/7 SRE included.
cost_model_assumptions: GPU unit economics derived from current runtime-1.20 cost sheet (link in attachments);
Assume buffer credit redemption rate 30% in first 60 days, tapering to 12% after steady state;
Preemption of spot/backfill resources for autoscale reduces marginal cost by ~45% but increases tail-latency risk.
Operational overhead for failover lanes estimated at 0.8 FTE per 200 reserved customers during onboarding and 0.2 FTE ongoing.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Internal dry run: validate billing pipes, quota enforcement, and console UI flows (Mar 15 - Mar 22).
Phase 1 - Closed pilot (5 enterprise customers): test BufferPool and FlexReserve; collect telemetry on redemption, latencies, and revenue impact (Apr 1 - Jun 30).
Phase 2 - Beta open to Sales: enable on-demand quoting for high-intent leads and gather contract negotiation data (Jul - Sep).
Phase 3 - GA: publish SKUs, docs, and pricing sheet; enable self-serve purchase for SteadyBand tiers (Q4).
stakeholder_feedback: Eng (Jin Park) 2026-03-04: Buffer credits require KV cache isolation changes; we can implement token accounting in the runtime but need one sprint for infra work.
Legal (Priya Singh) 2026-03-05: Customer-facing SLA language must clarify failover lanes are not equivalent to guaranteed throughput; require explicit contract annex for continuity credits.
Sales (Marco Ruiz) 2026-03-07: Sales prefers predictable 'blocks' over percent-based buffers; large customers want a mechanism to convert unused buffer credits to future discounts.
Finance (Lena Cho) 2026-03-09: Recommend initial price multipliers of 1.35x for overage on SteadyBand to offset risk and encourage BufferPool adoption.
engineering_notes: Runtime change: add token-level buffer accounting and a 'credit consume' API endpoint; requires DB schema migration Q1.
Autoscale: need to wire preemptible GPU hooks and add an autoscale budget controller to enforce burst block limits.
Observability: add per-customer buffer redemption metrics, burst frequency, and failover-route counts to Console dashboards.
Approx implementation estimate: 3 sprints (runtime + billing + console).
customer_concerns: Clarity on how buffer credits interact with regional failures and multi-region failover.
How long unused buffer credits carry forward and whether they are refundable on contract termination.
Risk that autoscale bursts will produce bad tail-latency for user-facing apps; need explicit guidance.
open_questions: How should unused buffer credits be treated at renewal? Convert to discount, expire, or rollover?
What concrete SLA credit formula do we use for BufferPool when failover lanes are invoked?
Should burst blocks be sold as fixed monthly bundles or auctioned at time of need?
Is security_review_required for failover lanes using customer-specific routing (yes/no)?
decisions: Decided to pilot BufferPool and FlexReserve in closed pilot with 5 customers before broader rollout (2026-03-11).
Agreed on three-month expiry for initial buffer credits in pilot to simplify accounting and avoid long tail liabilities.
Require legal annex that explicitly states failover lanes are lower priority and may be rate-limited during cloud outages.
